title.zh: 卷四百八十四 列傳第二百四十三 周三臣 韓通 李筠 李重進
title.en: Volume 484 Biographies 243: Three Zhou Officials Han Tong, Li Yun, Li Zhongjin
title.raw: 卷四百八十四 列傳第二百四十三 周三臣 韓通 李筠 李重進 Volume 484 Biographies 243: Three Zhou Officials Han Tong, Li Yun, Li Zhongjin

sentences.zh: 周三臣○韓通李筠李重進

translations.literal: Three Zhou Officials ○ Han Tong, Li Yun, Li Chongjin
translations.idiomatic: Three Zhou Officials — Han Tong, Li Yun, and Li Chongjin

sentences.zh: 《五代史記》有《唐六臣傳》，示譏也。

translations.literal: The Historical Records of the Five Dynasties has a "Biographies of the Six Tang Ministers," which was meant to show ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu's Historical Records of the Five Dynasties includes a "Biographies of the Six Tang Ministers" — a work meant as satire.

sentences.zh: 《宋史》傳周三臣，其名似之，其義異焉，求所以同，則歸於正名義、扶綱常而已。

translations.literal: The History of Song treats the Three Zhou Officials; the title sounds similar, but the meaning is different. What they have in common comes down to correcting names and principles and upholding moral order.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Song devotes a chapter to the Three Zhou Officials: the title echoes Ouyang's work, yet the intent differs. What the two share is a commitment to set names right and uphold the moral order.

sentences.zh: 韓通與宋太祖比肩事周，而死於宋未受禪之頃，然不傳於宋，則忠義之誌何所托而存乎？

translations.literal: Han Tong served Zhou on equal footing with the Song founder, yet died just before Song received the abdication. If he were not recorded in Song history, where would the record of loyalty and righteousness find a place to endure?
translations.idiomatic: Han Tong had stood shoulder to shoulder with the future Song founder in service to Zhou, only to die on the eve of the Song succession. Had the Song history not taken him up, where would posterity have kept the memory of his loyalty?

sentences.zh: 李筠、李重進舊史書叛，叛與否未易言也，洛邑所謂頑民，非殷之忠臣乎？

translations.literal: Li Yun and Li Chongjin were labeled rebels in the old histories; whether they were rebels is not easy to say. Were not the so-called "stubborn people" of Luoyi in fact loyal subjects of Yin?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories called Li Yun and Li Chongjin rebels, yet the charge is far from clear. Were not those whom the Zhou called the "stubborn people" of Luoyi in truth loyalists of the fallen Shang?

sentences.zh: 孔子定《書》，不改其舊稱焉。

translations.literal: When Confucius fixed the Book of Documents, he did not change its old designations.
translations.idiomatic: When Confucius edited the Book of Documents, he left its original designations intact.

sentences.zh: 或曰：三人者嚐臣唐、晉、漢矣。

translations.literal: Someone may say: these three men once served Tang, Jin, and Han.
translations.idiomatic: One might object that all three had once served the Tang, the Jin, and the Han.

sentences.zh: 曰：智氏之豫讓非歟！

translations.literal: The reply is: was not Yu Rang of the Zhi clan such a man!
translations.idiomatic: The answer is Yu Rang of the house of Zhi — was he not such a man?

sentences.zh: 作《周三臣傳》。

translations.literal: I compose the "Biographies of the Three Zhou Officials."
translations.idiomatic: Here I write the Biographies of the Three Zhou Officials.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，周祖為樞密使，統兵伐河中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyou reign, the Zhou founder was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and commanded troops to attack Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening year of Qianyou, the future Zhou founder, then Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, led an army against Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 知通謹厚，命之自隨，先登，身被六創，以功遷本軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Knowing Tong to be careful and honest, he ordered him to follow in person. Tong was first to scale the wall, suffered six wounds on his body, and for his merit was promoted to chief adjutant of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Tong prudent and steadfast, he kept him at his side. Tong was first over the wall, took six wounds, and was promoted to chief adjutant of the army for his valor.

sentences.zh: 周祖鎮大名，奏通為天雄軍馬步軍都校，委以心腹，及入汴，通甚有力焉。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder held Daming, he memorialized to appoint Tong commander of the Tianxiong Army's horse and foot forces, entrusted him as a confidant, and when he entered Bian, Tong was of great help.
translations.idiomatic: While stationed at Daming, the Zhou founder had Tong made commander of the Tianxiong horse and foot forces and treated him as a trusted confidant. When he marched into Bian, Tong proved indispensable.

sentences.zh: 授奉國左第六軍都校，領雷州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of the Left Sixth Army of the Fengguo Corps and concurrently served as prefect of Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the Left Sixth Army of the Fengguo Corps and given concurrent charge of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，為虎捷右廂都校，遷左廂，充孟州巡檢，繼領永、睦二州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, he became commander of the Right Wing of the Tiger Swift Corps, was transferred to the Left Wing, served as inspector of Mengzhou, and then held the posts of defense commissioner of Yong and Mu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangshun he commanded the right wing of the Tiger Swift Corps, then the left, served as inspector of Mengzhou, and afterward held the defense commissions of Yong and Mu.

sentences.zh: 周祖親征兗州，以通為在京右廂都巡檢。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder personally campaigned against Yanzhou, he made Tong chief inspector of the Right Wing in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the Zhou founder's personal campaign against Yanzhou, Tong was named chief inspector of the capital's right wing.

sentences.zh: 時河溢，灌河陰城，命通率廣銳卒千二百浚汴口，又部築河陰城，創營壁。

translations.literal: At that time the river overflowed and flooded Heyin city. He ordered Tong to lead twelve hundred elite troops of the Guangrui Corps to dredge the Bian estuary, and also to supervise the rebuilding of Heyin city and the construction of ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst its banks and inundated Heyin, Tong was sent with twelve hundred Guangrui elite troops to dredge the Bian mouth, rebuild Heyin, and raise new fortifications.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜保義軍節度觀察留後，周祖親郊，正授節度。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed military governor and observation commissioner designate of the Baoyi Army; when the Zhou founder performed the suburban sacrifice, Tong received full appointment as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made acting military governor of the Baoyi circuit, and received the full commission when the Zhou founder offered the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 并州劉崇南侵，命通副河中王彥超出晉州道擊之，敗於高平。

translations.literal: Liu Chong of Bingzhou invaded southward. Tong was ordered to assist Wang Yanchao of Hezhong in striking him along the Jinzhou route, but they were defeated at Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong of Bingzhou marched south, Tong was sent under Wang Yanchao of Hezhong to intercept him by way of Jinzhou; the force was beaten at Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 以通為太原北面行營部署，為地道攻其城。

translations.literal: Tong was made commander of the northern field headquarters against Taiyuan and attacked the city by tunnel.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was placed in command of the northern field headquarters against Taiyuan and besieged the city with mining tunnels.

sentences.zh: 俄班師，移鎮曹州，檢校太保。

translations.literal: Before long the army withdrew. He was transferred to garrison Caozhou and given the honorary title of Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: The army soon withdrew. Tong was reassigned to Caozhou and given the honorary rank of Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 世宗征淮南，命通為京城都巡檢。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, he appointed Tong chief inspector of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Shizong's Huainan campaign, Tong was made chief inspector of the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗以都城狹小，役畿甸民築新城，又廣舊城街道。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong found the capital too cramped, conscripted people of the capital region to build a new city, and also widened the streets of the old city.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the capital too cramped, Shizong pressed the metropolitan peasantry into building a new outer city and widening the old city's streets.

sentences.zh: 命左龍武統軍薛可信、右衛上將軍史佺、右監門衛上將軍蓋萬、右羽林將軍康彥環分督四面，通總領其役。

translations.literal: He ordered Xue Kexin, commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army; Shi Quan, senior general of the Right Guard; Gai Wan, senior general of the Right Gate Guard; and Kang Yanhuan, general of the Right Forest Guard, each to supervise one side, while Tong oversaw the whole project.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Kexin of the Left Dragon Martial Army, Shi Quan of the Right Guard, Gai Wan of the Right Gate Guard, and Kang Yanhuan of the Right Forest Guard were each assigned one quarter of the work, with Tong directing the entire undertaking.

sentences.zh: 功未就，世宗幸淮上，留通為在京內外都巡檢、權點檢侍衛司。

translations.literal: Before the work was finished, Emperor Shizong went to the Huai region and left Tong as chief inspector inside and outside the capital and acting inspector of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The project was still unfinished when Shizong went south to the Huai. Tong remained in charge of security throughout the capital and served as acting inspector of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 是役也，期以三年，才半歲而就。

translations.literal: This project had been scheduled for three years, yet was completed in only half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Though the work was budgeted for three years, it was finished in six months.

sentences.zh: 三年，追敘秦、鳳功，改領忠武軍節度、檢校太傅，又改侍衛馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: In the third year, his merits at Qin and Feng were recognized retrospectively. He was transferred to the Zhongwu military governorship and made Honorary Grand Tutor, and was also changed to chief adjutant of the Palace Guard horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his victories in Qin and Feng were belatedly honored: he was made military governor of Zhongwu, Honorary Grand Tutor, and chief adjutant of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸壽春，為京城內外都巡檢。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong visited Shouchun, Tong served as chief inspector inside and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizong was at Shouchun, Tong again held chief inspection duties for the entire capital.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，為歸德軍節度。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, he became military governor of the Guide Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Huainan was pacified, he was appointed military governor of Guide.

sentences.zh: 太祖奉詔北征，至陳橋為諸軍推戴。

translations.literal: The founder, on imperial orders for a northern campaign, reached Chenqiao and was acclaimed by the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The future Song founder marched north under imperial orders; at Chenqiao the troops acclaimed him as emperor.

sentences.zh: 通在殿閣，聞有變，惶遽而歸。

translations.literal: Tong was in the palace halls. Hearing of the upheaval, he hurried home in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was at the palace when news of the coup reached him. He rushed home in panic.

sentences.zh: 軍校王彥升遇通於路，策馬逐之，通馳入其第，未及闔門，為彥升所害，妻子皆死。

translations.literal: The army officer Wang Yansheng met Tong on the road, spurred his horse in pursuit, and Tong galloped into his residence. Before the gate could be shut, Yansheng killed him, and his wife and children all died.
translations.idiomatic: The officer Wang Yansheng overtook Tong in the street and chased him home. Tong reached his gate but could not bar it in time; Yansheng killed him, and his wife and children perished as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞通死，怒彥升專殺，以開國初，隱忍不及罪。

translations.literal: When the founder heard of Tong's death, he was angry that Yansheng had killed on his own authority, but because it was the founding of the dynasty, he restrained himself and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The founder was furious that Yansheng had killed Tong on his own authority, yet in the turmoil of founding the dynasty he swallowed his anger and imposed no punishment.

sentences.zh: 即下詔曰：“易姓受命，王者所以應期；

translations.literal: He immediately issued an edict saying: "A change of surname and receipt of the Mandate is how a true king answers the age;
translations.idiomatic: He at once issued an edict: "To change the ruling house and receive Heaven's Mandate is how a true king answers his time;

sentences.zh: 臨難不苟，人臣所以全節。

translations.literal: facing peril without compromise is how a minister preserves his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: to face peril without compromise is how a loyal minister keeps his integrity whole.

sentences.zh: 故周天平軍節度、檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事、侍衛親軍馬步軍副指揮使韓通，振跡戎伍，委質前朝，彰灼茂功，踐更勇爵。

translations.literal: The late Han Tong, military governor of the Zhou Ping Army, Honorary Grand Commandant, Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and deputy commander of the Palace Guard horse and foot forces, rose from the ranks of arms, pledged himself to the former dynasty, displayed outstanding merit, and repeatedly received brave titles.
translations.idiomatic: The late Han Tong — military governor of Ping, Honorary Grand Commandant, Grand Councilor, and deputy commander of the Palace Guard — rose from the ranks, gave his allegiance to the former dynasty, won conspicuous honors, and climbed again and again through the grades of martial distinction.

sentences.zh: 夙定交於霸府，遂接武於和門，艱險共嚐，情好尤篤。

translations.literal: Long ago he formed a bond in the founder's headquarters, then served together at the Gate of Harmony, shared hardships, and their friendship was especially close.
translations.idiomatic: We had sealed our friendship in the days of the military headquarters and served together at the Gate of Harmony, sharing every hardship; our bond was especially deep.

sentences.zh: 朕以三靈眷佑，百姓樂推，言念元勳，將加殊寵，蒼黃遇害，良用憮然。

translations.literal: I, by the favor of the three spirits and the willing acclaim of the people, was mindful of this founding merit and about to grant special favor, when he met sudden death — truly a cause for deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: By the favor of Heaven, earth, and the spirits, and with the people's willing acclaim, I had meant to honor this founding companion with exceptional favor — only to learn that he had been struck down in sudden violence. My grief is profound.

sentences.zh: 可贈中書令，以禮收葬。

translations.literal: Let him be posthumously made Director of the Secretariat and buried with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously appointed Director of the Secretariat and buried with full state honors.

sentences.zh: 遣高品梁令珍護喪事。”

translations.literal: Send the senior attendant Liang Lingzhen to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The senior attendant Liang Lingzhen is dispatched to supervise the funeral.

sentences.zh: 通性剛而寡謀，言多忤物，肆威虐，眾謂之“韓瞠眼”。

translations.literal: Tong's nature was stern and he lacked strategy; his words often offended others, and he indulged in cruelty and oppression. People called him "Han Stare-Eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Tong was rigid and short on counsel; his speech often gave offense, and he ruled by intimidation. Men nicknamed him "Han Stare-Eyes."

sentences.zh: 其子頗有智略，幼病傴，人目為“橐駝兒”。

translations.literal: His son was quite resourceful, but from childhood suffered a hunchback; people called him "the Camel Boy."
translations.idiomatic: His son was clever and far-seeing, though crippled from childhood by a hunchback; people called him "the Camel Boy."

sentences.zh: 見太祖有人望，常勸通早為之所，通不聽。

translations.literal: Seeing that the founder commanded popular esteem, he often urged Tong to act against him early, but Tong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the founder's rising prestige, the son repeatedly urged Tong to deal with him while there was still time, but Tong refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 後太祖幸開寶寺，見通及其子畫像於壁，遽命去之。

translations.literal: Later, when the founder visited Kaibao Temple and saw portraits of Tong and his son on the wall, he immediately ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on a visit to Kaibao Temple, the founder came upon wall portraits of Tong and his son and ordered them taken down at once.

sentences.zh: 李筠，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Li Yun was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun came from Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 善騎射。

translations.literal: He excelled at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 後唐秦王從榮判六軍諸衛，募勇士為爪牙，筠操弓矢求見。

translations.literal: When the Later Tang Prince of Qin, Congrong, administered the Six Armies and various guards, he recruited brave men as his personal followers. Yun came bearing bow and arrows to seek an audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Tang Prince of Qin, Li Congrong, took charge of the Six Armies and the palace guards, he recruited bold fighters as his personal retainers. Yun presented himself with bow in hand.

sentences.zh: 弓力及百斤，府中無能挽者，從榮令筠射，引滿有餘力，再發皆中，因以隸麾下。

translations.literal: His bow drew a hundred jin; no one in the prince's household could draw it. Congrong ordered Yun to shoot: he drew to the full with strength to spare, and both shots hit the mark. He was therefore enrolled under the prince's command.
translations.idiomatic: His bow required a draw of a hundred jin — none in the prince's household could bend it. Congrong had him shoot: Yun drew to the full with power to spare and hit the mark twice. The prince took him into his service.

sentences.zh: 從榮難作，筠騎從至天津橋，射殺十數人，知事不濟，棄馬遁去。

translations.literal: When Congrong's crisis broke out, Yun rode with him to Tianjin Bridge and shot down more than ten men. Seeing that the affair would not succeed, he abandoned his horse and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Congrong's rebellion collapsed, Yun rode with him to Tianjin Bridge and killed more than ten men with his bow. Realizing the cause was lost, he abandoned his horse and escaped.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，應募為內殿直，遷控鶴指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, he volunteered for the Inner Palace Guard and was promoted to commander of the Crane Control Corps.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qingtai reign he enlisted in the Inner Palace Guard and rose to command the Crane Control Corps.

sentences.zh: 晉開運末，契丹犯汴京，其將趙延壽聞筠驍勇，召置帳下。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin Kaiyun reign, the Khitans attacked Bianjing. Their general Zhao Yanshou, hearing of Yun's valor, summoned him and placed him under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jin Kaiyun era the Khitans stormed Bianjing. Their general Zhao Yanshou, hearing of Yun's prowess, took him into his retinue.

sentences.zh: 及契丹主北歸，死欒城，延壽至常山，為永康王所縶。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler returned north, he died at Luancheng. Yanshou reached Changshan and was seized by the Prince of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan emperor withdrew north, he died at Luancheng. Yanshou reached Changshan only to be seized by the Prince of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 契丹眾數萬，據常山，後北去。

translations.literal: Khitan forces numbering tens of thousands held Changshan, then later withdrew north.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Khitans held Changshan before eventually marching north.

sentences.zh: 留耶律解裏，眾才二千騎，又分別部首領楊袞以千騎掠邢、洺。

translations.literal: They left Yelü Heli with only about two thousand horsemen, and also detached the tribal leader Yang Gun with a thousand riders to raid Xing and Ming prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: They left Yelü Heli with barely two thousand horsemen and detached the tribal chief Yang Gun with a thousand riders to raid Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 來還中朝士大夫多在城中，契丹與漢相雜，解裏性貪恣自奉，削漢軍日食，眾皆菜色。

translations.literal: When they returned, many court scholars and officials were still in the city. Khitans and Chinese were intermingled. Heli was greedy and indulged himself, cutting the Chinese troops' daily rations until all were gaunt with hunger.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they returned, many court officials were still trapped in the city, Khitans and Chinese living side by side. Heli was greedy and self-indulgent; he cut the Chinese troops' rations until the men were hollow with hunger.

sentences.zh: 筠乘其怨，密與王蕘、石公霸、何福進等謀，以閏七月二十九日伺契丹守閽者旦食，撞寺鍾為期，相率入據兵庫，次焚牙門，大呼市人，並力擊焉。

translations.literal: Yun took advantage of their resentment and secretly plotted with Wang Rao, Shi Gongba, He Fujin, and others. On the twenty-ninth day of the intercalary seventh month they waited until the Khitan gate guards were at their morning meal, struck the temple bell as the signal, led one another in to seize the armory, then burned the headquarters gate, called loudly to the townspeople, and together pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Yun exploited their anger and secretly plotted with Wang Rao, Shi Gongba, He Fujin, and others. On the twenty-ninth of the intercalary seventh month, while the Khitan gate guards were at breakfast, they rang the temple bell as signal, seized the armory, set fire to the headquarters gate, roused the townspeople, and struck together.

sentences.zh: 契丹眾大驚，由北門而出，解裏趣族乘列之於野。

translations.literal: The Khitan host was greatly alarmed and went out through the north gate. Heli hurried his clan and baggage train and drew them up in formation in the open field.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans panicked and fled through the north gate. Heli rallied his clan and baggage train and formed them up in the open country.

sentences.zh: 明日集眾入郛力戰，屬晉士卒分掠，唯控鶴一軍與市民禦之，死傷相繼。

translations.literal: The next day he gathered his forces and entered the suburbs to fight fiercely. Jin soldiers were meanwhile out plundering on their own, so only the Crane Control Corps and the townspeople defended the city; casualties fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he massed his troops and fought into the suburbs. Jin soldiers were off looting on their own, leaving only the Crane Control Corps and townspeople to hold the line; the dead and wounded mounted without pause.

sentences.zh: 午後，郛外民千餘知契丹奔敗者，持兵趣其族乘，將劫之，守者入郛馳告，解裏聞之，遂挈族而去。

translations.literal: In the afternoon, more than a thousand people outside the suburbs, learning that the Khitans were fleeing in defeat, took up arms and rushed toward the clan and baggage train to plunder them. The guards entered the suburbs at a gallop to report; when Heli heard this, he led his clan away.
translations.idiomatic: That afternoon, hearing the Khitans were in flight, more than a thousand suburban men took up arms and rushed the baggage train to loot it. The guards galloped back to report; Heli gathered his clan and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，筠建謀約諸將同力，控鶴左廂都校白再榮首匿於室不敢應，筠拔佩刀破幕引臂迫之，再榮不得已而行，諸將次第赴之。

translations.literal: At first, when Yun laid the plan and asked the generals to act together, Bai Zairong, commander of the Left Wing of the Crane Control Corps, hid in his room and dared not answer. Yun drew his sword, tore through the curtain, seized his arm, and forced him; Zairong had no choice but to go, and the other generals followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun first proposed the plot and called on the generals to join, Bai Zairong of the Crane Control Left Wing hid indoors and would not answer. Yun drew his sword, slashed through the curtain, seized his arm, and dragged him out; the others then fell in behind.

sentences.zh: 及契丹去，百姓死者二千餘人。

translations.literal: By the time the Khitans departed, more than two thousand common people had died.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Khitans left, more than two thousand civilians lay dead.

sentences.zh: 諸將互伐其功，筠詣故相馮道請權領節度事，道曰：“子主奏事而已，留後事當議功臣為之。”

translations.literal: The generals disputed one another's merits. Yun went to the former chief councilor Feng Dao and asked to take charge of the military governorship provisionally. Dao said: "You, sir, should merely memorialize the throne on affairs; the matter of acting military governor should be decided by choosing among the meritorious officers."
translations.idiomatic: The generals quarreled over credit. Yun went to the former chief councilor Feng Dao and asked to take provisional charge of the circuit. Dao replied, "You need only memorialize the throne on current affairs; the acting governorship should go to whichever officer the court deems most deserving."

sentences.zh: 道恐諸將爭功復亂，乃以再榮前職貴加諸將，權推為留後，人心遂定。

translations.literal: Dao feared that the generals' dispute over merit would bring chaos again, so he cited Zairong's former rank as higher than the others' and had him provisionally made acting military governor; popular sentiment then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing fresh turmoil from the merit dispute, Dao cited Zairong's senior former rank and had him provisionally named acting governor; order was restored.

sentences.zh: 是戰，筠功居多，即送款漢祖，以其子赴朝，漢祖深賞之。

translations.literal: In this battle Yun's merit was greatest. He immediately sent allegiance to the Han founder and sent his son to court; the Han founder greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: In this fight Yun's contribution had been greatest. He at once pledged allegiance to the Han founder and sent his son to court; the founder was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 以控鶴一軍力戰，優加賜與，授再榮留後，筠博州刺史。

translations.literal: Because the Crane Control Corps had fought hard, they received generous rewards: Zairong was made acting military governor, and Yun was made prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Crane Control Corps was richly rewarded for its fighting; Zairong received the acting governorship, while Yun was given only the prefecture of Bo.

sentences.zh: 筠以賞薄不悅。

translations.literal: Yun was displeased that the reward was so meager.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was bitterly dissatisfied with so slight a reward.

sentences.zh: 周祖鎮大名，表為先鋒指揮使，又為北面緣邊巡檢。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder held Daming, he memorialized to appoint Yun vanguard commander and also made him northern frontier inspector.
translations.idiomatic: While the Zhou founder was stationed at Daming, he had Yun made vanguard commander and northern frontier inspector.

sentences.zh: 周祖起兵入汴，筠同郭崇從，與慕容彥超戰於留子陂，彥超東奔。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder raised troops and entered Bian, Yun followed with Guo Chong. They fought Murong Yanchao at Liuzi Slope, and Yanchao fled east.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder marched on Bian, Yun followed with Guo Chong, routed Murong Yanchao at Liuzi Slope, and drove him east in flight.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，權知滑州，俄真拜義成軍節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was made acting prefect of Huazhou, and soon received formal appointment as military governor of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangshun he was made acting prefect of Hua, then formally appointed military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 數月，改彰德軍節度。

translations.literal: A few months later he was transferred to the Zhangde military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was transferred to the Zhangde command.

sentences.zh: 會並人侵晉州，王峻率師往拒，筠亦請西征，詔褒之。

translations.literal: When the Bingzhou forces invaded Jinzhou, Wang Jun led an army to resist. Yun also requested a western campaign, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Han invaded Jinzhou, Wang Jun marched to meet them. Yun too petitioned for a western campaign and received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 又乞免黃澤關商稅，奏可。

translations.literal: He also asked exemption from commercial taxes at Huangze Pass, and the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also secured approval to abolish commercial taxes at Huangze Pass.

sentences.zh: 周祖征兗，還次濮，筠因朝，獻馬，賜襲衣、金帶。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder campaigned against Yan and halted at Pu on his return, Yun came to audience, presented horses, and was granted a ceremonial robe and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: On the Zhou founder's Yan campaign he halted at Pu on the return march; Yun attended court, presented horses, and received a ceremonial robe and gold belt.

sentences.zh: 從至澶，宴訖遣還。

translations.literal: He accompanied the founder to Chan, and after the banquet was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the founder as far as Chan; after the feast he was dismissed to his post.

sentences.zh: 及召潞州常思入朝，命筠權知軍府，思改宋、亳，以筠為昭義軍節度。

translations.literal: When Chang Si of Luzhou was summoned to court, Yun was ordered to take provisional charge of the military headquarters. Si was transferred to Song and Bo, and Yun was made military governor of the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Si of Luzhou was recalled to court, Yun was left in provisional command of the headquarters; Si was moved to Song and Bo, and Yun received the Zhaoyi military governorship.

sentences.zh: 三年，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the honorary title of Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 時王峻兼節製，以筠及王殷、何福進皆創業功臣，故並加恩焉。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Jun held concurrent command over several circuits. Because Yun, Wang Yin, and He Fujin were all founding merit-holders, they all received added favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun then held concurrent command over several circuits; Yun, Wang Yin, and He Fujin were all treated with extra favor as founders of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，周祖親郊，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, when the Zhou founder performed the suburban sacrifice in person, Yun was made Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiande, when the Zhou founder offered the suburban sacrifice in person, Yun was made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，並人入侵，其將張暉率先鋒自團柏穀入營梁侯驛，攻劫堡柵，所至焚略蕩盡，筠遣護軍穆令均率步騎二千拒之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, the Bingzhou forces invaded. Their general Zhang Hui led the vanguard from Tuanbai Valley into camp at Lianghou Post, attacked and plundered fortresses and stockades, and wherever he went burned and ravaged everything. Yun sent his guard general Mu Lingjun with two thousand foot and horse to resist.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong's accession the Northern Han invaded. Their general Zhang Hui led the vanguard through Tuanbai Valley to Lianghou Post, storming and looting every fort along the way until the countryside was scorched bare. Yun sent Mu Lingjun with two thousand infantry and cavalry to meet him.

sentences.zh: 令均營於太平驛，驛東南距潞八十里，失於偵邏，暉淩晨奄至，潞兵被甲介馬，暉見之佯退，潞兵追之，並伏遂發。

translations.literal: Lingjun encamped at Taiping Post, eighty li southeast of Luzhou. He failed in scouting and patrol. Hui arrived at dawn in a sudden attack. The Luzhou troops armored themselves and saddled their horses. When Hui saw them he feigned retreat; the Luzhou troops pursued, and the Bingzhou ambush then sprang.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjun camped at Taiping Post, eighty li southeast of Luzhou, but neglected his scouts. Hui struck at dawn. The Luzhou men armed and mounted; Hui feigned retreat, drew them in pursuit, and sprang his ambush.

sentences.zh: 令均且鬥且卻，步卒降並者數百人，騎不復者百人，餘眾還保潞。

translations.literal: Lingjun fought while retreating. Several hundred foot soldiers surrendered to the Bingzhou side; a hundred horsemen did not return. The rest withdrew to hold Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lingjun fought a fighting retreat. Hundreds of foot soldiers defected to the enemy; a hundred horsemen never returned. The survivors fell back on Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗親征沁州，降之，命筠率沁之行營兵赴太原，符彥卿戍忻口，拒契丹援兵。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong personally campaigned against Qinzhou and received its surrender. He ordered Yun to lead the Qinzhou field-army troops to Taiyuan, while Fu Yanqing garrisoned Xinkou to block Khitan reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong personally took Qinzhou and accepted its surrender. Yun was ordered to lead the Qinzhou field army against Taiyuan while Fu Yanqing held Xinkou against Khitan reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 彥卿請益師，詔筠與張永德以三千騎益之，既至，以偏師繞契丹後，奮擊走之。

translations.literal: Yanqing requested reinforcements. An edict ordered Yun and Zhang Yongde to add three thousand cavalry. When they arrived, a detached force circled behind the Khitans and struck fiercely, driving them off.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing asked for reinforcements; Yun and Zhang Yongde were sent with three thousand cavalry. They swung a flanking force behind the Khitans and drove them off in a sharp assault.

sentences.zh: 師還，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二年，筠破並軍於榆社，獲其將安濬、康超等七十餘人。

translations.literal: In the second year Yun defeated the Bingzhou army at Yushe and captured more than seventy of their officers, including An Jun and Kang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he routed the Northern Han at Yushe and took more than seventy officers, including An Jun and Kang Chao.

sentences.zh: 三年，筠遣行軍司馬範守圖率兵入遼州界，殺並卒三百餘，獲小校數人以獻。

translations.literal: In the third year Yun sent his campaign marshal Fan Shoutu with troops into Liaozhou territory, killed more than three hundred Bingzhou soldiers, and presented several junior officers captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he sent his campaign marshal Fan Shoutu into Liaozhou, killed over three hundred enemy troops, and presented several captured junior officers to court.

sentences.zh: 四年，又遣守圖入河東界，降二砦。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again sent Shoutu into Hedong territory and received the surrender of two stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Shoutu again raided into Hedong and took two stockades by surrender.

sentences.zh: 五年，筠自將入石會關，破並人六砦。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Yun personally led troops through Shihui Pass and broke six Bingzhou stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Yun led the assault through Shihui Pass and stormed six Northern Han stockades.

sentences.zh: 是冬，又破遼州長清砦，擒其磁州刺史李戴興以獻。

translations.literal: That winter he again broke the Changqing stockade in Liaozhou and captured its Cizhou prefect Li Daixing to present at court.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he took Liaozhou's Changqing stockade and sent its captured Cizhou prefect Li Daixing to the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄又敗並人於境，斬三百餘級。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again defeated the Bingzhou forces within his territory and beheaded more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he beat the enemy again within his borders and took more than three hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 六年，平遼州，獲刺史張丕旦等二百四十五人以獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he pacified Liaozhou and presented two hundred forty-five captives, including the prefect Zhang Pidan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he pacified Liaozhou and sent two hundred forty-five prisoners to court, including the prefect Zhang Pidan.

sentences.zh: 筠在鎮擅用征賦，頗集亡命，嚐以私忿囚監軍使，世宗心不能堪，但詔責而已。

translations.literal: While holding his command, Yun arbitrarily levied taxes and gathered many fugitives. He once imprisoned the army inspector over a private grudge. Emperor Shizong could not bear it in his heart, but only issued an edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: In his command Yun levied taxes on his own authority, gathered fugitives, and once imprisoned the army inspector in a private vendetta. Shizong was deeply displeased but issued only a reprimand.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi took the throne, Yun was made Honorary Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded, Yun was made Honorary Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 是秋，令裨將劉繼忠將兵與吐渾入並境，平賈家砦，斬百餘級，獲牛羊而還。

translations.literal: That autumn he ordered his lieutenant Liu Jizhong to lead troops with the Tuguhun into Bingzhou territory, pacified the Jia family stockade, beheaded more than a hundred, and returned with captured cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn his lieutenant Liu Jizhong led Tuguhun allies into Northern Han territory, took the Jia family stockade, killed over a hundred men, and returned with livestock.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆初，加兼中書令，遣使諭以受周禪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong under the founder, Yun was additionally made Director of the Secretariat. Envoys were sent to inform him of the Zhou abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianlong the founder additionally made him Director of the Secretariat and sent envoys to announce the Zhou succession.

sentences.zh: 筠即欲拒命，左右為陳曆數，方僶俛下拜，貌猶不恭。

translations.literal: Yun at once wished to refuse the order. Those around him set forth the mandate of Heaven, and only then did he bow reluctantly, yet his bearing was still disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was ready to refuse outright until his advisers pleaded the mandate of Heaven; he bowed only with reluctance, his manner still openly disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 及延使者升階，置酒張樂，遽索周祖畫像懸壁，涕泣不已。

translations.literal: When he detained the envoy and had him ascend the hall, he set out wine and music, then hastily demanded the Zhou founder's portrait and hung it on the wall, weeping without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When he detained the envoy and brought him up to the hall for wine and music, he suddenly demanded the Zhou founder's portrait, hung it on the wall, and wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 賓佐惶駭，告使臣曰：“令公被酒失其常性，幸勿為訝。”

translations.literal: His staff were alarmed and told the envoy: "Our commander is drunk and has lost his usual composure — please do not be surprised."
translations.idiomatic: His staff, horrified, told the envoy, "The commander is drunk and not himself — please do not take offense."

sentences.zh: 及太原劉鈞以蠟書結筠共舉兵，筠雖緘書上太祖，心已畜異謀，太祖手詔慰撫之。

translations.literal: When Liu Jun of Taiyuan sent a sealed wax letter to join with Yun in raising troops together, Yun though he sealed a letter and sent it up to the founder, already harbored a separate plot in his heart. The founder wrote a personal edict to comfort and reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jun of Taiyuan sent a sealed letter proposing a joint rebellion, Yun forwarded a loyal report to the founder even as he nursed treason in his heart. The founder answered with a personal edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 是時，筠子守節為皇城使，嚐泣諫，筠不聽。

translations.literal: At this time Yun's son Shoujie was commissioner of the Imperial City. He often wept and remonstrated, but Yun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's son Shoujie, then commissioner of the Imperial City, pleaded with tears again and again, but Yun would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 太祖又遣守節諭旨曰：“吾聞汝諫汝父，汝父不聽，吾今殺汝，何如汝歸語汝父，我未為天子時，任自為之，既為天子，獨不能臣我耶？”

translations.literal: The founder again sent Shoujie with an instruction, saying: "I hear you remonstrated with your father and he would not listen. I could kill you now — how would that be? Go back and tell your father: before I became Son of Heaven, he could do as he pleased; now that I am Son of Heaven, can he alone refuse to be my subject?"
translations.idiomatic: The founder sent Shoujie back with a message: "I hear you pleaded with your father and he would not listen. Shall I kill you instead? Go tell him this: when I was not yet emperor he could do as he liked; now that I am emperor, does he alone refuse to bow to me?"

sentences.zh: 守節白筠，筠謀愈甚，遂起兵，令幕府為檄書，辭多不遜。

translations.literal: Shoujie reported this to Yun. Yun's plotting grew fiercer, and he thereupon raised troops. He had his staff draft a proclamation, its language largely insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujie reported this to his father. Yun's conspiracy deepened; he raised an army and had his staff draft a proclamation full of defiant language.

sentences.zh: 從事閭丘仲卿獻策於筠曰：“公以孤軍舉事，其勢甚危，雖倚河東之援，亦恐不得其力。

translations.literal: His aide Lüqiu Zhongqing offered a plan to Yun, saying: "You are raising troops with an isolated force — the situation is very dangerous. Even if you rely on aid from Hedong, I fear you may not obtain its full strength."
translations.idiomatic: His aide Lüqiu Zhongqing urged him: "You are committing a lone army to rebellion — the odds are desperate. Even with Hedong's help, you may not get the support you need."

sentences.zh: 大梁兵甲精銳，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: The arms and armor of Daliang are keen and sharp — hard to contend with in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang's troops are superbly armed — you cannot hope to match them in open battle.

sentences.zh: 不如西下太行，直抵懷、孟，塞虎牢，據洛邑，東向而爭天下，計之上也。”

translations.literal: Better to march west down the Taihang, strike straight for Huai and Meng, block Tiger Cage Pass, seize Luoyang, and contend for the empire facing east — that would be the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: Better to descend the Taihang westward, seize Huai and Meng, block Tiger Cage Pass, hold Luoyang, and fight for the empire with your face to the east — that is the superior strategy.

sentences.zh: 筠曰：“吾周朝宿將，與世宗義同昆弟，禁衛皆舊人，聞吾之來，必倒戈歸我，況有儋珪槍、撥汗馬，何憂天下哉。”

translations.literal: Yun said: "I am an old general of the Zhou court, bound to Emperor Shizong like brothers by righteousness. The palace guards are all old comrades — when they hear I have come, they will surely turn their weapons and join me. Moreover, I have Dan Gui's spear and Bo Han's horse — why worry about the empire?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied: "I am a veteran of Zhou, sworn to Shizong like a brother. The palace guards are my old comrades — they will turn their spears to me at once. With Dan Gui's spear and Bo Han's horse, what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 儋珪，筠愛將，有勇力，善用槍；

translations.literal: Dan Gui was Yun's favorite general, brave and strong, skilled with the spear;
translations.idiomatic: Dan Gui was his favorite officer — strong, brave, and master of the spear;

sentences.zh: 撥汗，筠駿馬，日馳七百里，故筠誇焉。

translations.literal: Bo Han was Yun's fine steed, which could run seven hundred li in a day — hence Yun's boast.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Han was his charger, said to cover seven hundred li in a day — hence his boast.

sentences.zh: 執監軍亳州防禦使周光遜、閑廄使李廷玉，遣判官孫孚、衙校劉繼忠送於劉鈞求濟師。

translations.literal: He seized the army inspector, Bozhou defense commissioner Zhou Guangxun, and the idle-stable commissioner Li Tingyu, and sent his judge Sun Fu and guard officer Liu Jizhong to deliver them to Liu Jun to request reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the army inspector Zhou Guangxun of Bozhou and the stable commissioner Li Tingyu, and sent Sun Fu and Liu Jizhong to Liu Jun to beg for troops.

sentences.zh: 又遣人殺澤州刺史張福，往據其城。

translations.literal: He also sent men to kill Zezhou prefect Zhang Fu and went to seize that city.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Zezhou prefect Zhang Fu killed and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 劉鈞遂率兵與契丹數千眾來援，至太平驛，筠以臣禮迎謁，見鈞兵衛寡弱，甚悔之，而業已然矣。

translations.literal: Liu Jun then led troops with several thousand Khitans to aid him. When they reached Taiping Post, Yun received him with the rites due a subject. Seeing Jun's troops and guards few and weak, he deeply regretted it, but the deed was already done.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun marched to his aid with several thousand Khitans. Yun met him at Taiping Post with the deference of a vassal, then saw how few and weak Jun's troops were and bitterly regretted his choice — but it was too late.

sentences.zh: 鈞封筠西平王，賜馬三百匹，召與之語，筠自言受周祖大恩，敢愛死不寤。

translations.literal: Jun enfeoffed Yun as Prince of Xiping and gave him three hundred horses. Summoning him to speak, Yun said of himself that he had received great favor from the Zhou founder and dared not spare his life in waking loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made him Prince of Xiping and gave him three hundred horses. In private audience Yun declared that the Zhou founder's kindness bound him to give his life without flinching.

sentences.zh: 鈞與周祖有世仇，鈞默然，遂疑之。

translations.literal: Jun bore a hereditary feud with the Zhou founder. Jun fell silent and came to suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, who bore a hereditary feud with the Zhou house, said nothing — and began to doubt him.

sentences.zh: 命其宣徽使盧讚監筠軍，筠心不能平，頗與讚不協，鈞復命平章事衛融和解之。

translations.literal: He ordered his palace secretariat commissioner Lu Zan to supervise Yun's army. Yun could not accept this in his heart and was often at odds with Zan. Jun then ordered Grand Councilor Wei Rong to mediate between them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun appointed his palace commissioner Lu Zan to oversee Yun's army. Yun resented the intrusion and clashed with Zan until Jun sent Grand Councilor Wei Rong to patch the quarrel.

sentences.zh: 筠有馬三千匹，辟鞠場閱習，日夜謀畫為寇。

translations.literal: Yun had three thousand horses. He opened a polo ground for drill and day and night plotted raids.
translations.idiomatic: He kept three thousand horses, drilled them on a polo ground, and plotted rebellion day and night.

sentences.zh: 留其子守節守上黨，引眾南向。

translations.literal: He left his son Shoujie to hold Shangdang and led his forces south.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Shoujie to hold Shangdang, he marched south with his army.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣石守信、高懷德將兵討之。

translations.literal: The founder sent Shi Shouxin and Gao Huaide with troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The founder dispatched Shi Shouxin and Gao Huaide to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：“勿縱筠下太行，急進師扼其隘，破之必矣。”

translations.literal: An edict said: "Do not let Yun come down the Taihang. Press forward swiftly and hold the passes — you are sure to break him."
translations.idiomatic: The edict ran: "Do not let Yun descend the Taihang. Strike quickly and seal the passes — his defeat is certain."

sentences.zh: 又遣慕容延釗、王全斌由東路會守信，與監軍李崇矩破筠眾於長平，斬首三千級。

translations.literal: He also sent Murong Yanhao and Wang Quanbin by the eastern route to join Shouxin. Together with the army inspector Li Chongju they defeated Yun's forces at Changping and took three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanhao and Wang Quanbin were sent by the eastern route to join Shouxin. With the inspector Li Chongju they routed Yun at Changping and took three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 又攻大會砦，下之。

translations.literal: They also attacked the Dahui stockade and took it.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed and captured the Dahui stockade as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂親征。

translations.literal: The founder then campaigned in person.
translations.idiomatic: The founder took the field in person.

sentences.zh: 山路險峻多石不可行，太祖先於馬上負數石，群臣六軍皆負之，即日平為大道。

translations.literal: The mountain road was steep, perilous, and stony and could not be traveled. The founder first carried several stones on horseback; the ministers and the whole army all carried them, and that same day a level highway was made.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain track was steep and littered with boulders. The founder began by carrying stones from horseback; ministers and soldiers followed until a level road was cleared in a single day.

sentences.zh: 與守信、懷德會，破筠眾三萬於澤南，降者三千餘，殺筠監軍使盧讚，擒筠河陽節度範守圖，筠走還保澤。

translations.literal: He joined Shouxin and Huaide and defeated thirty thousand of Yun's troops south of Ze. More than three thousand surrendered. Yun's army inspector Lu Zan was killed, and his Heyang military governor Fan Shoutu was captured. Yun fled back to hold Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Shouxin and Huaide, he shattered thirty thousand of Yun's men south of Ze. Over three thousand surrendered; Lu Zan was killed and Fan Shoutu captured. Yun fled back into Ze.

sentences.zh: 太祖至，列柵圍之，筠龍捷使王廷魯、吐渾留後汾州團練使王全德率所部自昭義來降，筠益失援。

translations.literal: When the founder arrived, he set up stockades and besieged the city. Yun's Dragon Swift envoy Wang Tinglu and the Tuguhun regent, Fenzhou training commissioner Wang Quande, led their units from Zhaoyi to surrender. Yun lost support still further.
translations.idiomatic: The founder arrived and invested the city. Wang Tinglu of the Dragon Swift Corps and the Tuguhun regent Wang Quande of Fenzhou defected from Zhaoyi with their commands. Yun's isolation deepened.

sentences.zh: 太祖親督戰，拔其城，筠赴水死，獲鈞相衛融，鈞懼而遁歸。

translations.literal: The founder personally directed the assault, took the city, and Yun threw himself into the water and died. Jun's councilor Wei Rong was captured; Jun fled home in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The founder directed the final assault himself. The city fell; Yun drowned himself. Wei Rong, Liu Jun's councilor, was taken prisoner, and Jun fled north in terror.

sentences.zh: 太祖進伐上黨，守節以城降，釋其罪，賜襲衣、金帶、銀鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: The founder advanced to attack Shangdang. Shoujie surrendered the city. His crime was pardoned, and he was granted a ceremonial robe, gold belt, and horse with silver saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Shangdang, the founder accepted Shoujie's surrender, pardoned him, and rewarded him with a ceremonial robe, gold belt, and silver-trapped horse.

sentences.zh: 是日宴從官，守節預焉，以為單州團練使；

translations.literal: That day he feasted his attending officials; Shoujie was among them and was made training commissioner of Shanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: That evening he feasted his officers with Shoujie present and appointed him training commissioner of Shan;

sentences.zh: 以昭義軍節度副使趙處願為郢州刺史；

translations.literal: Zhaoyi deputy military governor Zhao Chuyuan was made prefect of Yingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chuyuan, deputy governor of Zhaoyi, was made prefect of Ying;

sentences.zh: 節度判官孫孚為屯田郎中；

translations.literal: military governor's judge Sun Fu was made director of the agricultural colonies bureau;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu, the governor's judge, was made director of the agricultural colonies bureau;

sentences.zh: 觀察判官史文通為水部郎中；

translations.literal: observation commissioner judge Shi Wentong was made director of the waterways bureau;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wentong, the observation judge, was made director of the waterways bureau;

sentences.zh: 前遼州衙內指揮使馬廷禹為右監門衛將軍，領壁州刺史。

translations.literal: former Liaozhou inner-palace commander Ma Tingyu was made general of the Right Gate Guard and concurrently prefect of Bizhou.
translations.idiomatic: and the former Liaozhou inner-palace commander Ma Tingyu was made general of the Right Gate Guard with concurrent charge of Bizhou.

sentences.zh: 筠性雖暴，事母甚孝，每怒將殺人，母屏風後呼筠，筠趨至，母曰：“聞將殺人，可免乎？

translations.literal: Though Yun's nature was violent, he was very filial toward his mother. Whenever in anger he was about to kill someone, his mother would call from behind the screen. Yun would hurry to her, and she would say: "I hear you are about to kill someone — can he be spared?
translations.idiomatic: For all his violence, Yun was deeply filial. Whenever rage drove him to execute someone, his mother would call from behind the screen. He would hurry to her side, and she would ask, "I hear you mean to kill someone — can he be spared?

sentences.zh: 為吾曹增福爾。”

translations.literal: It will add merit for us."
translations.idiomatic: It will bring us merit."

sentences.zh: 筠遽釋之。

translations.literal: Yun would at once release the prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yun would release the man at once.

sentences.zh: 筠稍知書，頗好調謔。

translations.literal: Yun had some learning and was fond of witty banter.
translations.idiomatic: Yun had some schooling and loved a jest.

sentences.zh: 初名榮，避周世宗諱，將改之，或令名“筠”，筠曰：“李筠，李筠，玉帛雲乎哉。”

translations.literal: His original name was Rong. To avoid the taboo on Emperor Shizong's name, he was to change it. Someone suggested the name "Yun." Yun said: "Li Yun, Li Yun — as if silks and jades were raining down!"
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Rong; to avoid Shizong's taboo he was to rename himself. When someone proposed "Yun," he quipped, "Li Yun, Li Yun — silks and jades raining from the sky!"

sentences.zh: 聞者皆笑。

translations.literal: All who heard laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who heard it laughed.

sentences.zh: 筠有愛妾劉氏，隨筠至澤，時被攻城危，劉謂筠曰：“城中健馬幾何？”

translations.literal: Yun had a favorite concubine, Lady Liu, who followed him to Ze. When the city was besieged and in peril, Liu said to Yun: "How many strong horses are there in the city?"
translations.idiomatic: His favorite concubine Lady Liu had followed him to Ze. As the siege tightened she asked, "How many sound horses remain in the city?"

sentences.zh: 筠曰：“爾安問此？”

translations.literal: Yun said: "Why do you ask this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Why do you ask?"

sentences.zh: 劉曰：“孤城危蹙，破在俄頃，今誠得馬數百，與腹心潰圍，出保昭義，求援河東，猶愈於坐待死也。”

translations.literal: Liu said: "This lone city is pressed to the brink; its fall is imminent. If we truly had several hundred horses, we could break out with trusted men, escape to hold Zhaoyi, and seek aid from Hedong — still better than sitting here awaiting death."
translations.idiomatic: She said, "The city is doomed within moments. With a few hundred horses and your closest men you could break out, reach Zhaoyi, and beg Hedong for help — better than waiting here to die."

sentences.zh: 筠然之。

translations.literal: Yun agreed that this was so.
translations.idiomatic: Yun agreed.

sentences.zh: 召左右計馬尚不減千匹，以是夕將出，或謂筠曰：“今帳前計議，皆云一心，縣門既發，不可保矣，倘劫公而降，悔其可及。”

translations.literal: He summoned his attendants to count the horses — still no fewer than a thousand — and planned to break out that night. Someone told Yun: "Those now deliberating before your tent all say they are of one mind, but once the city gate is opened, that cannot be guaranteed. If they seize you and surrender, regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants counted more than a thousand horses, and he planned a breakout that night. An adviser warned, "The men in council swear loyalty, but once the gate opens anything may happen. If they seize you and surrender, it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 筠猶豫不決。

translations.literal: Yun hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yun wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 明日城陷，筠將赴火，劉欲俱死，筠以其有娠，麾令去。

translations.literal: The next day the city fell. Yun was about to throw himself into the fire; Liu wished to die with him, but Yun, because she was pregnant, waved her away.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the city fell. Yun prepared to burn himself; Liu meant to die with him, but he sent her away because she was with child.

sentences.zh: 守節既購得之，果生子焉。

translations.literal: After Shoujie had ransomed and obtained her, she indeed bore a son.
translations.idiomatic: After Shoujie ransomed her, she did indeed bear a son.

sentences.zh: 字節字得臣，初補東頭供奉官。

translations.literal: His courtesy name was Jie and his style Dechen. He was first appointed eastern-head attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Courtesy name Jie, style Dechen. He began as an eastern-head palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，嚐以心疾乘醉擊殺供禦白鶻，筠上章待罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: During Guangshun, he once in a fit of mental illness, while drunk, struck and killed an imperial white crane kept for tribute. Yun submitted a memorial awaiting punishment, and an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangshun, in a drunken spell of madness he killed an imperial white crane. Yun submitted himself for punishment; an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 四遷至皇城使，曆單、濟二州團練使。

translations.literal: After four promotions he reached commissioner of the Imperial City and served in turn as training commissioner of Shan and Ji prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Four promotions brought him to commissioner of the Imperial City and training commands in Shan and Ji.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年，出知遼州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiande he was sent out to govern Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qiande he was posted to govern Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，改和州團練使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he was transferred to training commissioner of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao he was transferred to training commissioner of He.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年三十三。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year, aged thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 無後，以劉氏所生之弟為嗣。

translations.literal: He had no heir, so the younger son born to Lady Liu was made his successor.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir; the younger son Lady Liu had borne was adopted as his successor.

sentences.zh: 李重進，其先滄州人。

translations.literal: Li Chongjin — his ancestors were from Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongjin's family came originally from Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 周太祖之甥，福慶長公主之子也，生於太原。

translations.literal: He was the Zhou founder's nephew, son of the Princess of Fuqing, and was born in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew of the Zhou founder and son of the Princess of Fuqing, he was born in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，仕為殿直。

translations.literal: During the Jin Tianfu era he served as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Jin he served as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 漢初，從周祖征河中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he followed the Zhou founder in the campaign against Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Later Han he followed the Zhou founder against Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，遷內殿直都知，領泗州刺史，改小底都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was promoted to director of the Inner Palace Guard, held concurrent charge of Sizhou prefect, and was changed to commander of the Junior Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangshun he became director of the Inner Palace Guard, took charge of Sizhou, and was made commander of the Junior Guard.

sentences.zh: 二年，改大內都點檢、權侍衛馬步軍都軍頭，領恩州團練使，遷殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made chief inspector of the Inner Palace, acting commander-in-chief of the Palace Guard horse and foot forces, training commissioner of Enzhou, and then commander of the Palace Front Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he became chief inspector of the Inner Palace, acting head of the Palace Guard, training commissioner of En, and then commander of the Palace Front Army.

sentences.zh: 三年，加領泗州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was additionally given charge as defense commissioner of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he additionally received the Sizhou defense commission.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，領武信軍節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he held the Wuxin military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiande he held the Wuxin military governorship.

sentences.zh: 重進年長於世宗，及周祖寢疾，召重進受顧命，令拜世宗，以定君臣之分。

translations.literal: Chongjin was older than Emperor Shizong. When the Zhou founder lay gravely ill, he summoned Chongjin to receive the final charge, ordered him to bow to Shizong, and thereby fixed the distinction between ruler and subject.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin was older than Shizong. On his deathbed the Zhou founder summoned him, entrusted him with the succession, and made him bow to Shizong to fix their roles as sovereign and subject.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，為侍衛親軍馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Chongjin became chief adjutant of the Palace Guard horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizong's accession he became chief adjutant of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征劉崇，戰於高平，不利，大將樊愛能、何徽以其眾遁，唯重進與白重讚勒兵不動。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong in the campaign against Liu Chong. At Gaoping the battle went badly; the great generals Fan Aineng and He Hui fled with their troops. Only Chongjin and Bai Chongzan held their forces steady without moving.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizong's campaign against Liu Chong, the battle at Gaoping turned sour and generals Fan Aineng and He Hui fled with their men. Only Chongjin and Bai Chongzan held their lines firm.

sentences.zh: 既而太祖先以麾下犯敵，重讚繼領所部力戰，世宗躬率衛兵合勢，周師復振，崇遂大敗。

translations.literal: Then the founder first led his personal troops against the enemy; Chongzan followed leading his command in fierce fighting; Shizong personally led the guard troops to combine their strength; the Zhou army rallied again, and Chong was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Then the future Song founder struck with his household troops; Chongzan followed with a fierce assault; Shizong led the guards in person; the Zhou line rallied and Liu Chong was routed.

sentences.zh: 以功領忠武軍節度。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the Zhongwu military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he received the Zhongwu command.

sentences.zh: 及進討太原，又為行營馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: When they advanced to attack Taiyuan, he again served as chief adjutant of the field-army horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: On the advance against Taiyuan he again served as chief adjutant of the field army.

sentences.zh: 師還，加同中書門下平章事，改歸德軍節度兼侍衛馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was made Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, transferred to the Guide military governorship, and concurrently made commander of the Palace Guard horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made Grand Councilor, military governor of Guide, and commander of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 世宗親征淮南，命重進將兵先赴正陽。

translations.literal: When Shizong personally campaigned against Huainan, he ordered Chongjin to lead troops first to Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On Shizong's personal Huainan campaign, Chongjin was sent ahead to Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 俄聞李穀攻壽春不克，退保正陽，促重進兵助之。

translations.literal: Soon it was heard that Li Gu had failed to take Shouchun and had withdrawn to hold Zhengyang; Chongjin was urged to advance and assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Li Gu had failed at Shouchun and fallen back on Zhengyang; Chongjin was ordered to hurry to his aid.

sentences.zh: 吳人以穀退為懼，乃發兵三萬餘，旌旗輜重亙數百里；

translations.literal: The Wu, taking Gu's retreat as cause for alarm, then sent out more than thirty thousand troops; banners, baggage, and supply trains stretched for several hundred li;
translations.idiomatic: The Wu, emboldened by Gu's retreat, marched out more than thirty thousand men, their banners and baggage trains stretching for hundreds of li;

sentences.zh: 又發戰棹二百艘以張斷橋之勢，列陣鼓噪而北，橫布拒馬以萬數，皆貫以利刃，維以鐵索；

translations.literal: they also launched two hundred war boats to display the power to cut off the bridge, drew up battle lines with drums and shouts marching north, and laid out by the tens of thousands chevaux-de-frise all tipped with sharp blades and bound with iron chains;
translations.idiomatic: two hundred warships to block the crossing, battle lines advancing north with drums and shouts, and tens of thousands of chevaux-de-frise tipped with blades and linked by iron chains;

sentences.zh: 又刻木為戰形，立陣前，號“揵馬牌”，皮囊貯鐵蒺莉以布戰地。

translations.literal: they also carved wooden figures in the shape of warriors and set them before the lines, called "horse-blocking boards," and stored iron caltrops in leather bags to spread over the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: wooden warrior effigies set before the ranks — "horse-blocking boards" — and leather sacks of iron caltrops strewn across the field.

sentences.zh: 時周師未朝食，吳師奄至，周師望其陣皆笑之。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou army had not yet taken its morning meal when the Wu forces suddenly arrived. The Zhou troops looked upon their formation and all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou troops had not yet breakfasted when the Wu host appeared. The Zhou soldiers looked at the enemy array and laughed.

sentences.zh: 宣祖領前軍與重進、韓令坤合勢擊之，一鼓而敗，斬首萬餘級，追奔二十餘里，殺大將劉彥貞，擒裨將盛師朗數十人，降三千人，獲戈甲三十萬。

translations.literal: The founder led the vanguard and, combining strength with Chongjin and Han Lingkun, struck them. At the first drum they were broken; more than ten thousand heads were taken; the pursuit ran twenty-odd li; the great general Liu Yanzhen was killed; several tens of junior officers including Sheng Shilang were captured; three thousand surrendered; three hundred thousand weapons and armor were taken.
translations.idiomatic: The future Song founder led the van with Chongjin and Han Lingkun. One charge broke the Wu line: ten thousand heads, a pursuit of twenty li, the death of Liu Yanzhen, dozens of officers including Sheng Shilang captured, three thousand prisoners, and three hundred thousand sets of arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 世宗大悅，詔書褒諭，即以重進代穀為行營招討使，賜襲衣、金帶、玉鞍、名馬。

translations.literal: Shizong was greatly pleased. An edict praised and instructed him, and Chongjin was at once made field-army pacification commissioner in place of Gu, and granted a ceremonial robe, gold belt, jade saddle, and famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was delighted. An edict praised the victory and replaced Gu with Chongjin as pacification commissioner of the field army, granting him a ceremonial robe, gold belt, jade saddle, and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 三年，以重進為廬、壽等州招討使。

translations.literal: In the third year Chongjin was made pacification commissioner of Lu, Shou, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made pacification commissioner for Lu, Shou, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時李繼勳主壽春，重進駐軍城北，聞城南洞屋為淮人所焚，將議退軍。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jixun held Shouchun. Chongjin encamped north of the city. Hearing that the tunnel-works south of the city had been burned by the Huai men, he was about to discuss withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixun then held Shouchun while Chongjin camped north of the walls. When Huainan forces burned the southern siege tunnels, he was ready to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 會太祖自六合歸，道出壽州，因駐師旬餘，重進倚以為援，兵威復振。

translations.literal: It happened that the founder was returning from Liuhe and passed by way of Shouzhou, whereupon he halted his army for more than ten days. Chongjin relied on him as support, and military prestige rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: The founder was returning from Liuhe and halted at Shouzhou for more than ten days. Chongjin drew fresh confidence from his presence, and army morale revived.

sentences.zh: 吳人大懼，以重進色黔，號“黑大王”。

translations.literal: The Wu were greatly afraid. Because Chongjin's complexion was dark, they called him "the Black King."
translations.idiomatic: The Wu were terrified of him. His dark complexion earned him the name "Black King."

sentences.zh: 張永德屯下蔡，與重進不協。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongde was stationed at Xia'ai and was not on good terms with Chongjin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongde held Xia'ai and was on bad terms with Chongjin.

sentences.zh: 永德每宴將吏，多暴重進短，後乘醉謂重進有奸謀，將吏無不驚駭。

translations.literal: Whenever Yongde feasted his officers he often exposed Chongjin's faults. Later, while drunk, he said Chongjin harbored treacherous designs, and the officers were all alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: At every feast Yongde aired Chongjin's faults; once drunk he accused Chongjin of treason, to the horror of every officer present.

sentences.zh: 永德密遣親信乘驛上言，世宗不之信，亦不介意。

translations.literal: Yongde secretly sent a trusted man by post relay to report upward. Shizong did not believe it and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde sent a trusted courier by post to report the charge; Shizong did not believe it and took no notice.

sentences.zh: 二將俱握重兵，人情益憂恐。

translations.literal: Both generals held heavy forces, and popular sentiment grew ever more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Both generals commanded large forces, and anxiety spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 重進遂自壽陽單騎直詣永德帳中，命酒飲，親酌謂永德曰：“吾與公皆國家肺腑，相與戮力，同獎王室，公何疑我之深也。”

translations.literal: Chongjin then rode alone from Shouyang straight to Yongde's tent, ordered wine, and personally poured for him, saying: "You and I are both the state's own flesh and blood. We strive together and alike support the royal house — why do you suspect me so deeply?"
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin rode alone from Shouyang into Yongde's camp, called for wine, and poured for him himself: "We are both pillars of the state, fighting together for the throne — why do you doubt me so bitterly?"

sentences.zh: 永德意解，二軍皆安。

translations.literal: Yongde's mind was eased, and both armies were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde's suspicions melted away, and both armies were calmed.

sentences.zh: 李景知之，密令人齎蠟書誘重進，啖以厚利，重進表其事。

translations.literal: Li Jing learned of this and secretly sent a man bearing a sealed wax letter to entice Chongjin, tempting him with rich profit. Chongjin memorialized the matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Wu learned of the quarrel and sent a sealed letter tempting Chongjin with rich rewards. Chongjin reported the offer to court.

sentences.zh: 時行濠州刺史齊藏珍亦說重進，世宗知之，假他事誅藏珍。

translations.literal: At that time Qi Cangzhen, prefect of Hao on detached duty, also urged Chongjin. Shizong learned of it and executed Cangzhen on a pretext of another offense.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Cangzhen, acting prefect of Hao, also urged Chongjin to defect. Shizong learned of it and had Cangzhen executed on another charge.

sentences.zh: 詔重進夾淮城正陽、下蔡，既成，上其圖。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chongjin to build cities flanking the Huai at Zhengyang and Xia'ai. When they were finished, he submitted the plans.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to build fortified towns on the Huai at Zhengyang and Xia'ai and submitted the plans when they were complete.

sentences.zh: 俄又敗淮兵二千餘於塌山北。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again defeated more than two thousand Huai troops north of Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he routed more than two thousand Huainan troops north of Tashan.

sentences.zh: 時圍壽經年未下，吳遣將許文緽、邊鎬舟師數萬，溯淮來援。

translations.literal: The siege of Shou had gone on for a year without success. Wu sent the generals Xu Wenyun and Bian Hao with a fleet of tens of thousands, sailing up the Huai to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Shou had dragged on a year. Wu sent Xu Wenyun and Bian Hao upstream with a fleet of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 文緽維舟淮南，據紫金山，山距壽數里，設十餘砦，連亙相望，與城中烽火相應；

translations.literal: Wenyun moored his boats south of the Huai, seized Purple Gold Mountain — the mountain lay several li from Shou — and set up more than ten stockades in continuous sight of one another, coordinating with beacon fires in the city;
translations.idiomatic: Wenyun anchored south of the Huai and seized Purple Gold Mountain, a few li from Shou, where he built more than ten linked stockades in beacon contact with the city;

sentences.zh: 又南築夾道，將抵壽為饋路。

translations.literal: he also built a walled corridor to the south, intending to reach Shou as a supply route.
translations.idiomatic: and began a walled supply corridor southward toward the city.

sentences.zh: 重進伺其城北展砦，出兵擊之，敗五千餘眾，奪二砦，獲器甲甚眾。

translations.literal: Chongjin watched for them to extend stockades north of the city, then sent troops to strike. He defeated more than five thousand men, seized two stockades, and captured a great quantity of weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy extended stockades north of the city, Chongjin struck, killed more than five thousand, took two stockades, and captured a vast store of arms.

sentences.zh: 世宗幸壽，宴從官，召重進賜戎服、玉帶、金銀器、繒彩、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: Shizong visited Shou, feasted his attending officials, summoned Chongjin, and granted him military dress, jade belt, gold and silver vessels, silks, and horse with saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong visited Shou, feasted his officers, and rewarded Chongjin with military dress, a jade belt, gold and silver vessels, silks, and a trapped horse.

sentences.zh: 及克壽，錄功加檢校太傅兼侍中，又改天平軍節度，仍為招討使。

translations.literal: When Shou was taken, his merit was recorded: he was made Honorary Grand Tutor and Palace Attendant, transferred to the Tianping military governorship, and still remained pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou fell, his merit earned him Honorary Grand Tutor and Palace Attendant, the Tianping command, and retention of the pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 四年，攻取濠州南關城，其團練使郭廷謂以兵萬餘降，獲糧數萬斛。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he attacked and took the southern pass city of Haozhou. Its training commissioner Guo Tingyu surrendered with more than ten thousand troops, and tens of thousands of hu of grain were captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took Haozhou's southern pass; Guo Tingyu surrendered with more than ten thousand men and tens of thousands of hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 從平楚州，命先還揚州。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of Chuzhou and was ordered to return first to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Chuzhou and was ordered back to Yangzhou ahead of the main force.

sentences.zh: 五年，世宗在迎鑾，遣重進將兵赴廬州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Shizong was at Yingluan and sent Chongjin with troops to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, while Shizong was at Yingluan, he sent Chongjin to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 會李景請畫江為界，世宗遂還，留重進戍守，景遣人以牛酒來犒，俄乃還鎮。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Jing requested that the Yangzi be taken as the boundary. Shizong then returned, leaving Chongjin to garrison the region. Jing sent men with cattle and wine to reward the troops, and before long Chongjin returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing sued for peace with the Yangzi as boundary. Shizong withdrew, leaving Chongjin to garrison the frontier. Jing sent cattle and wine as gifts; Chongjin soon returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 六年，世宗北征，次博州，重進來朝，賜宴行宮，即命將兵先趣北面，及世宗駐瓦橋關，重進與諸將率師而至。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Shizong campaigned north, halted at Bozhou, and Chongjin came to audience and was feasted at the traveling palace. He was at once ordered to lead troops first toward the northern front. When Shizong halted at Waqiao Pass, Chongjin and the other generals led their armies up.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, on Shizong's northern campaign, Chongjin attended him at Bozhou and was feasted at the traveling palace, then sent ahead to the northern front. When Shizong reached Waqiao Pass, Chongjin arrived with the other generals and their armies.

sentences.zh: 時關南已平，議進取幽州，會世宗不豫而止。

translations.literal: At that time the southern passes had been pacified and there was discussion of advancing to take Youzhou, but it stopped when Emperor Shizong fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: The southern passes were pacified and the court debated an advance on Youzhou, but Shizong's illness brought the plan to a halt.

sentences.zh: 即命率所部赴河東，次百井路，敗並人五千餘，斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: He was at once ordered to lead his command to Hedong, halted at Baijing Road, defeated more than five thousand Bingzhou troops, and beheaded more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to Hedong, camped at Baijing Road, routed more than five thousand Northern Han troops, and took over two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 恭帝嗣位，加檢校太尉，改淮南道節度。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi succeeded, Chongjin was made Honorary Grand Commandant and transferred to the Huainan circuit military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: On Gong's accession he was made Honorary Grand Commandant and military governor of the Huainan circuit.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣石守信、王審琦、李處耘、宋偓四將率禁兵討重進。

translations.literal: The founder sent the four generals Shi Shouxin, Wang Shenqi, Li Chuyun, and Song Wo to lead palace troops against Chongjin.
translations.idiomatic: The founder sent Shi Shouxin, Wang Shenqi, Li Chuyun, and Song Wo with palace troops to suppress Chongjin.

sentences.zh: 會友規至，賜襲衣、金帶、器幣、鞍馬，以為滁州刺史，監前軍。

translations.literal: It happened that You Gui arrived. He was granted a ceremonial robe, gold belt, vessels and goods, saddle and horse, made prefect of Chuzhou, and appointed to supervise the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: You Gui arrived and was rewarded with a ceremonial robe, gold belt, gifts, and horse, then made prefect of Chu and supervisor of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂左右曰：“朕於周室舊臣無所猜間，重進不體朕心，自懷反側，今六師在野，當暫往慰撫之爾。”

translations.literal: The founder said to those around him: "Toward the old ministers of the Zhou house I harbor no suspicion. Chongjin does not understand my heart and nurses rebellion in his breast. Now the six armies are in the field — I should go for a time to comfort and reassure him."
translations.idiomatic: The founder told his attendants, "I suspect none of Zhou's old ministers. Chongjin has failed to read my intentions and turned rebellious. With the armies already in the field, I should go myself to reassure him."

sentences.zh: 遂親征，次大儀鎮。

translations.literal: He thereupon campaigned in person and halted at Dayi town.
translations.idiomatic: He marched in person and halted at Dayi.

sentences.zh: 石守信遣使馳奏，揚州破在旦夕，願車駕臨視。

translations.literal: Shi Shouxin sent a messenger at a gallop to report: Yangzhou would fall within the day; he wished the imperial carriage would come to oversee.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shouxin sent a courier at full speed: Yangzhou would fall within the day and he begged the emperor to come in person.

sentences.zh: 太祖徑至城下，即日拔之。

translations.literal: The founder went straight to beneath the walls and took the city that same day.
translations.idiomatic: The founder rode straight to the walls and took the city the same day.

sentences.zh: 初，城將陷，重進左右勸殺思誨，重進曰：“吾今舉族將赴火死，殺此何益。”

translations.literal: Earlier, when the city was about to fall, Chongjin's attendants urged him to kill Si Hui. Chongjin said: "My whole clan is now about to go to the fire and die — what good would killing him do?"
translations.idiomatic: As the city was falling, his men urged him to kill Si Hui. Chongjin said, "My whole clan is about to die by fire — what good would killing him do?"

sentences.zh: 即縱火自焚，思誨亦為其黨所害。

translations.literal: He then set the fire and burned himself. Si Hui was also killed by his faction.
translations.idiomatic: He set the fire and burned himself; Si Hui was killed by his own followers.

sentences.zh: 太祖入駐城西南，閱逆黨數百人，盡戮之。

translations.literal: The founder entered and encamped in the southwest of the city, reviewed several hundred rebels, and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The founder encamped in the southwest quarter, reviewed several hundred rebels, and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 重進兄深州刺史重興，聞其叛，自殺。

translations.literal: Chongjin's elder brother Chongxing, prefect of Shenzhou, on hearing of the rebellion killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chongxing, prefect of Shen, killed himself on hearing of the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 弟解州刺史重讚、子尚食使延福並戮於市。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chongzan, prefect of Jiezhou, and his son Yanfu, commissioner of the Imperial Kitchen, were both executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Chongzan of Jie and his son Yanfu, commissioner of the Imperial Kitchen, were both executed in public.

sentences.zh: 初，重進謀舉兵，遣親吏翟守珣往潞，陰結李筠。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chongjin plotted to raise troops, he sent his personal clerk Zhai Shouyun to Luzhou to join secretly with Li Yun.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongjin first plotted rebellion, he sent his clerk Zhai Shouyun to Luzhou to conspire secretly with Li Yun.

sentences.zh: 守珣素識太祖，往還京師，潛詣樞密承旨李處耘求見，太祖問曰：“我欲賜重進鐵券，彼信我乎？”

translations.literal: Shouyun had long known the founder. Traveling back and forth to the capital, he secretly sought an audience with Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Li Chuyun. The founder asked: "I wish to grant Chongjin an iron certificate of mercy — will he believe me?"
