translations.idiomatic: Shouyun knew the founder well. On a trip to the capital he secretly sought Li Chuyun and an audience. The founder asked, "If I grant Chongjin an iron certificate of mercy, will he trust me?"

sentences.zh: 守珣曰：“重進終無歸順之誌。”

translations.literal: Shouyun said: "Chongjin in the end has no intention of returning to allegiance."
translations.idiomatic: Shouyun replied, "Chongjin will never submit in good faith."

sentences.zh: 太祖厚賜守珣，許以爵位，且令說重進緩其謀，無令二凶並作，以分兵勢。

translations.literal: The founder richly rewarded Shouyun, promised him a noble rank, and also ordered him to persuade Chongjin to slow his plot, so that the two villains would not act together and thereby divide the military strength.
translations.idiomatic: The founder richly rewarded Shouyun, promised him rank, and sent him back to urge Chongjin to delay his plot so the two rebels would not rise together and split the imperial armies.

sentences.zh: 守珣歸，勸重進養威持重，未可輕發，重進甚信之。

translations.literal: Shouyun returned and urged Chongjin to build prestige and act with weight, and not to move rashly. Chongjin trusted him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyun returned and urged Chongjin to bide his time and not strike rashly. Chongjin trusted him completely.

sentences.zh: 及李筠誅，重進反書聞，並如太祖之策，其不信鐵券，亦如守珣所雲。

translations.literal: When Li Yun was executed and Chongjin's letter of rebellion was reported, everything matched the founder's strategy; that he would not trust the iron certificate was also as Shouyun had said.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yun was killed and Chongjin's rebellion was reported, events unfolded exactly as the founder had planned — including Chongjin's refusal to trust the iron certificate, just as Shouyun had predicted.

sentences.zh: 揚州既平，購得守珣，補殿直，俄為供奉官。

translations.literal: After Yangzhou was pacified, Shouyun was bought out with a reward, appointed a palace attendant, and soon made a tribute commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Yangzhou fell, Shouyun was found and rewarded with appointment as palace attendant, then tribute commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又有張崇詁者，周廣順初，為樞密承旨。

translations.literal: There was also Zhang Chonggu. At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun he was commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhang Chonggu, who at the start of Guangshun served as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為解州刺史、兩池權鹽使，多規畫鹽池利害。

translations.literal: In the second year he was sent out as prefect of Jiezhou and acting salt commissioner of the Two Pools, and planned much concerning the advantages and disadvantages of the salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was posted to Jie as prefect and acting salt commissioner of the Two Pools, drafting many plans for the salt works.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，改德州，又改泗州、澤州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande he was transferred to Dezhou, then again to Sizhou and Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande he was transferred to De, then to Si and Ze.

sentences.zh: 崇詁本名崇訓，恭帝嗣位，避諱改焉。

translations.literal: Chonggu's original name was Chongxun; when Emperor Gongdi succeeded, he changed it to avoid the taboo.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Chongxun; he changed it when Gong succeeded to avoid the imperial taboo.

sentences.zh: 重進赴淮南時，道出泗上，崇詁說以畜兵完城之計。

translations.literal: When Chongjin went to Huainan, his route passed Si. Chonggu urged on him the plan of gathering troops and completing the city defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongjin marched to Huainan he passed through Si, where Chonggu urged him to stock troops and fortify the city.

sentences.zh: 重進敗，事露，詔捕之，棄市，籍其家。

translations.literal: When Chongjin was defeated the affair was exposed. An edict ordered his arrest; he was executed in the marketplace and his household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongjin's defeat the plot came to light. An edict ordered his arrest; he was executed in public and his property confiscated.
